2A.8 We are to earnestly seek God.

precepts.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? Hope thou in God, for I shall yet praise him. David is saying I may be down but I am not out; I still have fight in me. Some of you run out the minute correction comes. Correction is a good thing: it keeps you on your toes, makes you stronger, and Moses said to correct some openly so others fear. Never keep yes-men around you; a man in your circle who cannot correct you hates you and is waiting for your downfall, and the same goes for the sister who will not tell you what you want to hear.
precepts.point: Some of you will betray the brother next to you out of fear, because Esau threatens to tell the congregation what you were watching; your mind was in porn instead of the scriptures. With AI they will set many of us up with fake video, and some of our own people will believe it with no proof because they never built their minds in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear”. When fear or trouble tries to put you down, David shows how to talk to your own soul: “Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.”

David is speaking to himself, to his soul. Put plain: I might be down, but I'm not broken. I might be down, but I'm not out yet. Satan tried to take me out, but I'm still fighting. My hope is in the Lord, and I still have some fight in me.

Some of you are quick to give up. As soon as something happens, you run out: why did they have to put correction? Correction is a good thing. It keeps you on your toes, it makes you better and stronger. What doesn't break you makes you stronger; that is correction, that is the word of God. You can use a brother's correction to build yourself up: in my mind I was going to do what this brother got corrected for, so let me move from it. Moses said some you correct openly, so that others fear. Some of you never were corrected in your life until you came to IUIC, and you are too prideful to take it.

Brothers, never keep a yes-man around you. If you have a man in your circle who cannot say, bro, I don't think you should do this, that man hates you and is waiting for your downfall. You want men who tell you, don't talk evil of leadership; if you have a problem with a brother, go to him. Sisters are the same: the sister who won't tell you what you want to hear is not your enemy, she is the one you want around you, because she has no respect of persons. Men like that help you get the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.text: Job's soul is poured out; the days of affliction take hold of him, his bones are pierced in the night, and God has become cruel to him and opposes himself against him, bringing him to the grave, the house appointed for all living. This is the same situation David was in: the Lord was opposed to him for his sin and did not listen at some point, but after David turned around, the Lord began to listen.
precepts.point: As with a sword in his bones, his enemies reproach him while they say daily, "Where is thy God?" Again he preaches to his soul: "Why art thou cast down? Hope thou in God, for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God."

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

precepts.why:
“As with a sword in my bones, mine enemies reproach me”. Job knew that place: “My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.” “And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.” He is cast into the mire, become like dust and ashes, and worse: “I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not. Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.” He knows the Lord “wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living”, the grave.

This is the same situation David was in. The Lord was opposed to him for his sin and did not listen at some point; but after David turned around, the Lord began to listen. That is why David can preach to his own soul, “hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him”. Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High: when affliction comes we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. This is the situation a lot of us end up in if we lose sight of what we are supposed to be doing, which is keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: This was the issue with the Israelites coming against David and speaking evil of him: he turned away from sin, yet they reproached him for it, so he asked the Lord to requite them.
precepts.point: This is the situation a lot of us end up in if we lose sight of what we are supposed to be doing, which is keeping the commandments.

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

precepts.why:
“mine enemies reproach me; while they say daily unto me, Where is thy God?” Ecclesiasticus shows what was wrong with that: “Reproach not a man that turneth from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.”

This was the issue with the Israelites coming against David and speaking evil of him. He had turned away from sin, yet they reproached him for it, as if they were not all worthy of punishment themselves. So he asked the Lord to requite them. The one who has turned from sin is not to be reproached; he is to hope in God.

precepts.text: The Most High will go and return to his place until they acknowledge their offence and seek his face; in their affliction they will seek him early.
precepts.point: Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High. This is Hosea 5:15; when affliction comes we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. Even people in the world call on the Lord when things go wrong, though he does not always hear them.

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

precepts.why:
“Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God”. Hosea shows why the affliction comes and what it does: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The Most High goes and returns to his place until they acknowledge their offence and seek his face, and in their affliction they seek him early.

Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High. When affliction comes, we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. Even people in the world call on the Lord when things go wrong, though he does not always hear them. For David, cast down with a sword in his bones, the affliction is what turned him back to hope in God, “who is the health of my countenance, and my God.”

precepts.text: When Absalom sought the kingdom, David let Shimei curse him, saying the Lord had bidden him to curse, and "it may be that the Lord will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord will requite me good for his cursing this day." The Lord is the one who allowed the cursing, and through the affliction received from man, David would be repaid good. Being cursed and afflicted, we receive a reward for overcoming it.
precepts.point: Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High. This is Hosea 5:15; when affliction comes we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. Even people in the world call on the Lord when things go wrong, though he does not always hear them.

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

precepts.why:
David's enemies reproached him daily, and he had lived it before. When Absalom sought the kingdom and Shimei cursed him, David said, “so let him curse, because the Lord hath said unto him, Curse David.” “Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord hath bidden him. It may be that the Lord will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord will requite me good for his cursing this day.”

The Lord is the one who allowed the cursing, and through the affliction received from man, David would be repaid good. That is how to hear “Where is thy God?” from the mouths of the enemy: being cursed and afflicted, we receive a reward for overcoming it. So the soul is not to be cast down but to hope in God, “for I shall yet praise him”.

moments.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

points: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? Hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God. The Bible acknowledges emotional suffering, despair, and discouragement. Why is your soul cast down? Why don't you have any hope? Why do you turn to alcohol? Hope thou in God.

People say it isn't that simple. It is simple: you put your hope in the bottle, and you prove it because you do it every day and can't stop. The same way you are faithful to that bottle is how you are supposed to be doing the word of God: reading every day, desiring wisdom.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

points: As the hart pants after the water brooks, so David's soul pants after God. A hart is a deer; the panting is drinking up water. His soul thirsts for the living God, and he asks when he shall come and appear before God.

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

points: His tears have been his meat day and night, while his enemies continually say to him, "Where is thy God?" This is the same mockery as in Micah 7: because he is afflicted, they ask where his God is.

points: When David remembers these things he pours out his soul, remembering how he went with the multitude to the house of God with the voice of joy and praise, with a multitude that kept holy day.

points: "Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts; all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me." The waves are the affliction; all the Lord's afflictions have gone over him.
